title: The Singhpuria misl

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Nishanwalias, who carried the Dal Khalsa's standard: the flag-bearers. Today, the band of a man who carried a fan.

The man with the fan. Earlier on this path you met him at Amritsar, fanning the sangat on a hot day, when the title of nawab found him. Nawab Kapur Singh went on to lead the Khalsa through the hard years. But the title came to a man who already had home ground: his own village, his own riders, and they had a name. Today, not the title and not the fan. Today: the Singhpuria misl.
screen: `THE MAN WITH THE FAN.` → `A LEADER OF EVERYONE.` → `AND HIS OWN RIDERS.`

segments.voice: Three pieces. A renamed village: tradition says Kapur Singh took a village called Faizullapur, near Amritsar, and renamed it Singhpura, the town of the Singhs. His band took the new name, the Singhpurias, and some histories still call them by the old one, the Faizullapurias. The misl's name holds a small act of claiming. The size of the band: in the way Sikh histories tell it, the Singhpurias were not among the great misls in riders or land. That's the surprise. The man who held the title of nawab, whom the chiefs followed through the hard century, led a modest band of his own. He could have used his place at the head of the Khalsa to make his own riders the strongest. Tradition doesn't remember him doing that. Who came after: when Kapur Singh grew old, tradition says, the leadership of the whole Khalsa did not pass to his own band. It went to Jassa Singh, of the Ahluwalias, the rider he had trained. His misl carried on under its own chiefs, and the leadership of everyone went where he judged it should go. A nawab whose band stayed modest. A chief who handed the biggest job outside his own circle. Sikh histories dwell on his humility: the fan, the stables, the robe touched to the feet of five Sikhs. The Singhpuria misl is the same humility, written in the map. The nawab's band.
screen: `FAIZULLAPUR RENAMED SINGHPURA.` · `A MODEST BAND FOR A NAWAB.` · `THE LEADERSHIP PASSED OUTSIDE IT.` · `HUMILITY WRITTEN IN THE MAP.` · then, large: `THE NAWAB'S BAND.`

segments.voice: Think of a time you could have kept something and handed it on instead: a seat, a role, the last slice, a job a newer person got to try. Or a time you held on; don't judge either, just let the moment come back, what it cost you and what it gave them. If you pray, breathe Waheguru as it settles.

howItsDone: Sikhs remember Nawab Kapur Singh in Sikh histories and gurdwara talks as a leader known for seva, and the Singhpuria misl as the band that came from his village.

notes: This day avoids retelling day 852 (the fan and the title) and recalls it in a line.
Faizullapur renamed Singhpura by Kapur Singh, and 'Singhpura' glossed as 'the town of the Singhs': confirm.
'Not among the great misls' is a comparative claim framed as Sikh histories' telling; confirm or cut.
Leadership of the Dal Khalsa passing to Jassa Singh Ahluwalia rather than within the Singhpuria misl (which passed to his nephew Khushal Singh in common accounts, not named here): confirm.
'The robe touched to the feet of the Five' recalls day 852's telling ('five respected Sikhs'); confirm wording.
